Structurally, the designation precedes a surah dominated by warning, force, and measured requital, while mercy is doubled in two forms. The packet supplies that ordering; I infer that the opening name assigns the coming acts to a merciful governing source rather than making mercy merely one later topic. The basmala therefore reads as a framing act: even severe episodes are narrated under a twice-marked economy of mercy.

The conditional sequence moves from visual reception to bodily refusal and then to a verbal relabeling. The packet supplies those stages; I infer that calling the sign “magic” is the cognitive instrument that permits the side-turn. The ayah reads as a causal anatomy of denial, not merely a list of reactions.

The sign’s opponents may call the alleged magic either passing/transient or recurrent/continuing. Later recurrent punishments and the parallel `نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ` keep both branches active: I infer no need to force one duration. Their label can dismiss the sign as something that will pass while also alleging a repeated, sustained deception.

The ayah reads as a spatial-temporal hinge: leave them, until they must move toward the call.

The ayah’s image is therefore resurrection-as-dispersal, not dispersal after a separately stated resurrection.
